shape: Each object in traits is one habit, element, attachment, radius or organ need. Fields: trait (parameter path, or 'organ:<name>' when no parameter exists), need (the value or structure the palm requires), outcome (reachable | unreachable-value | unsupported-anatomy), capability (the hyphenated gate name when this need is a named capability, else null), depends_on (an existing open spec id, or null), confidence (high | medium | unsure), note (the reading from the trait space). required_capabilities is the same list written on the manifest engineering row.

traits.need: 1, a single trunk, matching the profile's single-stemmed oasis or orchard palm
traits.note: HabitParams.stems validates 1..=6. The stem is an axis. capabilities() always emits woody-axes for a registered preset. Date-palm is not registered, so the gate will still list woody-axes as missing.

traits.need: 0, a stem that stations no laterals (Corner's unbranched monopodial axis)
traits.note: lateral_orders validates as <= 8, so 0 is legal. scaffold.rs stations laterals only when axis.order < lateral_orders, so 0 never calls station() on the leader. Attractors pull the leader heading and do not add laterals. This is a value, not a missing capability, so it is not in required_capabilities.

traits.need: 0 laterals at a station, if that were the only dial
traits.note: Validates 1..=12, and scaffold.rs uses laterals_per_station.max(1) on the leader. The palm does not need this dial at 0, because lateral_orders=0 never places a station. Recorded so a reader who only looks at this range does not file a false gap.

Unit range 0..=1. Named models are regions of this space (fn-24). Corner as a habit region is reachable. The complete Corner form also needs the apical leaf crown, which is a separate attachment need.

traits.need: 0, a trunk of near-constant diameter, no pipe-model thickening from distal load
traits.note: resolved() keeps length_taper.max(0.0). On an unbranched axis, shed is 0 everywhere when taper is 0, each node's r is 1 before scale, and the stem scales to trunk_radius * height. The solve is still a pipe model; the mature column is the product. There is no trait that names the absence of a cambium. That mechanism is not asked. The visual constant diameter is.

traits.need: fronds borne only as a rosette at the apex of a thick unbranched stem, with no laterals and no twig clothing of the trunk
traits.note: place() and bearing_runs() clothe slender wood and twig-marked runs. shoot_radius is a fraction of root radius: on a constant-diameter trunk, a value below 1 clothes nothing and 1 clothes the whole stem. short_shoot_radius skips wood thicker than its fraction. twigs.generations validates 1..=6, so a twig layer always exists; a childless tip above trunk_height still gets a terminal twig, which is a small shoot bearing the family's one blade, not a crown of fronds. No canopy row means 'apex only'.

traits.need: one pinnate frond: leaflets along a rachis, one placement
traits.note: build_element draws one simple blade or needle. lobe_count 0..=8 cuts the margin toward the midrib; it is not a leaflet count. FoliageUnit is Leaf or Needle. fn-33 (open) adds leaflet_count, rachis_length, leaflet_pitch and terminal_leaflet and expands a placement along a drawn rachis. The ash proof is the same pinnate grouping. Scale is a value (element.length allows up to 1e3 m). Not a new gap.

traits.need: basal leaflets of the Phoenix frond modified as spines
traits.note: No element or organ row distinguishes a spine from a leaflet. fn-33 names leaflet count and pitch, not a spinose basal leaflet. flowctl specs --json shows no open spec for acanthophyll or leaflet spines. Pine's paired-needle-fascicle is the same disposition, a different organ.

traits.need: retained petiole bases clothing the trunk as a 3D organ, the diamond boots of a date palm
traits.note: The spec lists this as an organ, not as bark. No attachment or element trait places a retained leaf base on the stem. surface.lobes and the material plate and furrow rows can texture bark. Whether a bark-plate look would be accepted as this organ is unsure; the organ itself has no trait. No open spec names it.

traits.need: a hanging date cluster from the crown
traits.note: fn-33 (open) specifies one reproductive organ slot for a flower, a cone or a fruit, placed at stations as a second foliage list. That is the existing spec for a fruiting organ. Unsure whether a branched Phoenix spadix is one hanging organ element or a structure the single-element slot cannot draw. Not filed as a new gap. fn-33's own boundary parks a second fruit slot (oak acorns).

classes.reason: The date cluster adds realism; the palm is recognisable without it (two of the three reference photographs show fruitless crowns), and fn-33's organ slot serves many species. The owner put the palm's date clusters in the backlog on 2026-09-24.
